adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:18 — Tests renamed to TestIntegration* and skipped under -short, so the unit CI run no longer exercises cleanup at all and a broken delete path would go green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly renames the tests to `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp` / `TestIntegrationOldAnnotationsAreDeletedFirst` and adds `if testing.Short() { t.Skip(...) }` at the top of each, so any test run using `-short` will skip these cleanup assertions. That’s a concrete reduction in test coverage for the cleanup/delete paths. However, the claim that the “unit CI run” uses `-short` and that cleanup is no longer exercised at all can’t be verified from the diff alone (there may be other tests or different CI flags).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — Placeholder path is unbounded for MySQL/Postgres, so a batch size above 65535 fails every cleanup cycle with a parameter-limit error (only SQLite is guarded).

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteByIDs`, non-SQLite databases always use one `?` placeholder per ID (`placeholders := "?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)` and `args = asAny(ids)`) with no upper bound. With a large `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`, `fetchIDs` can return that many IDs, producing a statement with that many bind parameters. The diff only guards SQLite (inlining IDs if batch size > 999) and does not cap/partition batches for MySQL/Postgres, so sufficiently large batch sizes can reliably trigger driver/DB parameter-limit errors and make cleanup fail repeatedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:656 — Loop stops when a delete affects 0 rows even if fetchIDs returned ids (e.g. concurrently deleted by another HA instance), silently abandoning the remaining backlog until the next tick.

adjudication.rationale: In the new two-step batching, `untilDoneOrCancelled` decides it is “done” based on the *delete*’s `RowsAffected()` count, not on whether there is more work to do. Each batch does `ids, _ := r.fetchIDs(...)` then `x, y := r.deleteByIDs(..., ids)` and returns `x` (affected) to `untilDoneOrCancelled`. If another instance deletes those same `ids` after the fetch, `deleteByIDs` can return `0` affected even though `fetchIDs` returned a non-empty batch and there may still be additional matching rows beyond this batch. The loop will stop on `affected == 0`, prematurely ending the cleanup pass until the next scheduler tick.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:528 — Fetch-then-delete runs in separate sessions without a transaction, so a failure after some batches leaves partial deletion and orphaned tags if the orphan-tag pass then errors.

adjudication.rationale: In the new cleanup logic, each batch does `fetchIDs()` in one `r.db.WithDbSession(...)` and then `deleteByIDs()` in a separate `WithDbSession(...)`, with no surrounding transaction (see `untilDoneOrCancelled` callbacks in `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`). This makes the cleanup non-atomic across steps/batches: if an error occurs after some batches (or between annotation deletion and orphan-tag cleanup), the DB can be left in a partially-cleaned state with remaining orphaned tags until a later run. The diff comments suggest eventual consistency is acceptable, so this is more a consistency/robustness concern than a clearly incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:241 — Tests insert explicit IDs via InsertMulti, which does not advance the Postgres sequence, so later auto-ID inserts on the shared test DB can hit duplicate-key errors.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `createTestAnnotations` now sets `ID: int64(i+1)` and bulk-inserts via `sess.InsertMulti(...)`, meaning rows are inserted with explicit primary keys rather than letting the DB/sequence assign them. The diff does not show any sequence reset on cleanup (only `DELETE FROM annotation` / `annotation_tag`), and the same `fakeSQL := db.InitTestDB(t)` is reused across subtests in `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`. While the diff doesn’t prove a subsequent auto-ID insert happens in this file, the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded test-isolation risk on Postgres where sequences typically won’t advance when explicit IDs are provided, potentially causing later inserts (elsewhere using the same DB) to reuse IDs and hit duplicate-key errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:99 — The 40003-row SQLite-limit case only exercises the inline-values branch on SQLite; on MySQL/Postgres it doesn't test the parameter-limit risk and just adds slow inserts.

adjudication.rationale: The new test case `"should not fail if batch size is larger than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER..."` creates 40003 annotations and sets `annotationCleanupJobBatchSize: 32767`. In production code, the special handling is in `deleteByIDs`: it only switches to inline `IN (1,2,3,...)` values when `r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`. So this case specifically exercises that SQLite-only branch; on MySQL/Postgres it will still use placeholders (`?, ?, ...`) and thus doesn't validate any non-SQLite parameter-limit behavior, while still incurring very large inserts/deletes in an integration test. This is a concrete test-scope/performance concern, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:276 — require.NoError inside the WithDbSession callback, which then returns nil, hides real insert errors behind a FailNow in the callback instead of propagating the error.

adjudication.rationale: In createTestAnnotations, the WithDbSession callbacks do call require.NoError(t, err) inside the loop and then `return nil`. However, `require.NoError` triggers `t.FailNow` (via runtime.Goexit) on error, so the callback will not continue to the `return nil` path and the test will fail with the real insert error. The diff does not show an error being silently swallowed/hidden by returning nil after a failed insert.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Debug logging left at Error level on every batch (including successful/empty ones) and dumps the full ID list (up to batch size), flooding error logs every cycle.
matched_golden_ids: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that non-error/debug information is being logged at Error level, which will flood/pollute production error logs. The candidate adds details (every batch, full ID list) but the underlying issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Cleanup ticker silently changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, a 10x increase in cleanup job frequency and DB load unrelated to the stated fix.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go changes the ticker interval from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`, which is a 10x increase in how often the cleanup loop runs. This is a concrete, behavior-changing modification visible in the PR and appears unrelated to the annotation cleanup changes, raising a legitimate scope/performance concern even if it may be intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — Non-SQLite path binds one placeholder per ID, so batch sizes above the Postgres (65535) or MySQL prepared-statement parameter limits make every cleanup batch fail.

adjudication.rationale: The new `deleteByIDs` implementation builds an `IN` clause with one `?` placeholder per ID for all non-SQLite DBs (`placeholders := "?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)`), and `ids` length is driven by `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` via the `LIMIT(...)` in `fetchIDs`. There is no guard/chunking for Postgres/MySQL parameter limits, so configuring a batch size larger than those limits would make `session.Exec` fail for every batch. The diff only adds a workaround for SQLite (parameter limit 999), not for other dialects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:608 — The inline-vs-placeholder choice keys off the configured batch size instead of len(ids), so it only works because fetched IDs never exceed the batch size.

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteByIDs`, the SQLite inlining decision uses `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999` rather than `len(ids) > 999` (or similar). In this diff, all callers fetch `ids` via `fetchIDs` with a `LIMIT(r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize)`, so `len(ids)` will not exceed the batch size, making the current behavior effectively safe. However, the helper is brittle/incorrect if reused with an `ids` slice larger than the batch size or if the fetch logic changes, and it may inline IDs unnecessarily when `batch size > 999` but `len(ids) <= 999`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:241 — The test now inserts explicit annotation IDs, which leaves Postgres sequences behind and can cause duplicate-key failures for later inserts that use the default ID in the same DB.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `createTestAnnotations` to set explicit primary keys (`ID: int64(i + 1)`) before inserting (`sess.InsertMulti(...)`). In Postgres, inserting explicit IDs does not automatically advance the backing sequence, so later inserts that rely on the default/sequence can eventually collide once the sequence catches up to an existing ID. The diff does not show such a later default-ID insert occurring in this test, so it’s not a directly verifiable failing bug here, but it is a concrete test-isolation/fragility concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Leftover debug logging at Error level dumps full ID lists and SQL conditions on every batch, including successful ones.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple `r.log.Error(...)` calls inside the normal cleanup loop (e.g., in `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`) that execute on every batch regardless of success, and include full `ids` slices and the generated `cond` string. This will emit error-level logs for expected behavior and can dump very large ID lists (batch size can be 32767 per the new test/config), causing log spam and potential performance/operational impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:576 — Tag cleanup has the same leftover Error-level debug logs, which flood logs with every ID it touches.

adjudication.rationale: In `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`, the diff adds `r.log.Error` calls that log normal cleanup progress and include the full `ids` slice (`r.log.Error("Tags to clean", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, ...)` and a similar line after deletion). Since this runs in a loop (`untilDoneOrCancelled`) and can process many IDs per batch, it can flood logs and incorrectly mark routine work as errors. This is a concrete, diff-grounded operational issue rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Cleanup ticker went from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no explanation; this looks like a leftover debug change, not an intended tuning.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go changes the cleanup loop ticker from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`, which materially increases how often the cleanup job runs. The diff provides no accompanying comment or contextual change to justify the tuning, so it’s a concrete, diff-grounded concern about potentially unintended behavior/performance impact rather than a provable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:528 — The fetch, log, delete, log closure is copied three times (by time, by count, orphaned tags) instead of being pulled into one helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows essentially the same inline `untilDoneOrCancelled` callback pattern repeated in three places: `CleanAnnotations` (MaxAge branch), `CleanAnnotations` (MaxCount branch), and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`—each builds a `cond`, calls `r.fetchIDs(...)`, logs, calls `r.deleteByIDs(...)`, and logs again. This is not a correctness defect, but it is a concrete maintainability issue introduced by the change and could reasonably be refactored into a shared helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:536 — Names like x, y hide that the values are the affected count and the error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `x, y := r.deleteByIDs(...)` and returns/logs them as affected/error, but this is purely a naming/readability nit (no functional defect or concrete review issue beyond style).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:608 — The SQLite inline-ID branch depends on the configured batch size rather than len(ids), and builds the string with repeated O(n^2) Sprintf calls.

adjudication.rationale: In deleteByIDs, the SQLite branch triggers when r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999, not when len(ids) > 999 (the actual placeholder count). This is visible in: `if r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit { ... }`. Since ids are fetched with SQL LIMIT using that same batch size, this won’t cause incorrect behavior, but it can force unnecessary inline-ID SQL even when len(ids) <= 999. Also, the inline list is built via repeated `fmt.Sprintf` in a loop (`values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`), which is O(n^2) and can be a performance concern for large batches (e.g., 32767 IDs as tested).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:607 — The hardcoded 999 SQLite parameter limit contradicts the test name, which refers to the 32766 limit in SQLite 3.32+.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a mismatch between the test intent/name and the implementation comment/constant: the new test case is named "should not fail if batch size is larger than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER for SQLite >= 3.32.0" and uses batch size 32767, while `deleteByIDs` hardcodes `sqliteParameterLimit = 999` with a comment "SQLite has a parameter limit of 999." This is a documentation/expectation inconsistency rather than a functional defect (the code intentionally bypasses placeholders when batch size > 999, so the test would still pass), but the finding is valid as a specific, diff-grounded review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:529 — fetchIDs takes a raw SQL fragment that includes ORDER BY/LIMIT as its "condition", which leaks query construction into callers.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `fetchIDs(ctx, table, condition)` builds `SELECT id FROM <table> WHERE <condition>` (new function in `xorm_store.go`). Callers pass `cond` strings that include not just predicates but also `ORDER BY` and dialect-specific `LIMIT`/`LIMIT OFFSET` fragments, e.g. `cond := fmt.Sprintf(`%s AND created < %v ORDER BY id DESC %s`, annotationType, cutoffDate, r.db.GetDialect().Limit(...))`. This works syntactically, but it confirms the finding: query-shaping logic (ordering/limiting) is pushed into the caller while the parameter is named/treated as a WHERE-condition, which is an API/architecture concern introduced by this change rather than a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:274 — The batched InsertMulti loop is duplicated for annotations and tags, and the magic batchsize 500 is repeated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show two similar batched InsertMulti loops in createTestAnnotations (one for newAnnotations and one for newAnnotationTags), each with a local `batchsize := 500`. However, this is a maintainability/style refactor suggestion (deduping code / avoiding a repeated magic constant), not a defect or a substantively important non-bug issue grounded in new behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Every cleanup batch logs at Error level with the full slice of IDs (up to batch size), creating massive log volume and misleveled noise.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple `r.log.Error(...)` calls inside the per-batch cleanup loops (e.g., in `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`) that log `"ids", ids` for each batch. Since these run repeatedly via `untilDoneOrCancelled`, this will emit Error-level logs on normal successful operation and can include up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` IDs, creating large log volume and noisy/misleveled errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:576 — Orphaned-tag cleanup logs every batch at Error level including full ID lists, flooding logs on each run.

adjudication.rationale: In `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`, the new batching loop logs with `r.log.Error(...)` both before and after deletion (e.g., "Tags to clean" and "cleaned tags"), and includes the full `ids` slice in the log fields. This happens regardless of whether an error occurred (the `err` field is logged even when nil). That can unnecessarily emit Error-level logs and potentially flood logs with large ID lists on every cleanup run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Cleanup job ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute, running all cleanup jobs (annotation scans, deletes) 10x more often with material DB load.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go changes the ticker from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`, which will trigger the cleanup loop 10x more frequently. This is a verifiable behavioral/operational change that can increase DB/IO load, but it’s not inherently a correctness defect based solely on the diff (it may be intentional).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:611 — SQLite ID-list building uses repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is quadratic in batch size (e.g. 32767 IDs).

adjudication.rationale:
In `deleteByIDs` (added in this diff), the SQLite path for large batches builds an `IN (...)` string via repeated `fmt.Sprintf` concatenation:

```go
values := fmt.Sprint(ids[0])
for _, v := range ids[1:] {
  values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)
}
```

This pattern reallocates and copies the growing string each iteration, which is quadratic in the number of IDs; the new test case uses `annotationCleanupJobBatchSize: 32767`, making this a potentially significant performance issue. It’s not a correctness defect (the SQL should still be valid), but it is a concrete diff-grounded inefficiency introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:549 — Max-count cleanup uses LIMIT with OFFSET MaxCount each batch, forcing the DB to scan and skip MaxCount rows per iteration.

adjudication.rationale: In `CleanAnnotations` when `cfg.MaxCount > 0`, each batch builds `cond := fmt.Sprintf(`%s ORDER BY id DESC %s`, annotationType, r.db.GetDialect().LimitOffset(r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, cfg.MaxCount))` and then calls `r.fetchIDs(...)` repeatedly via `untilDoneOrCancelled`. This keeps applying the same `OFFSET cfg.MaxCount` on every iteration, so the DB must skip the first `MaxCount` rows each batch (an OFFSET-based pagination pattern), which can be inefficient for large `MaxCount`. The diff shows this behavior; it’s a performance/algorithmic concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Debug output logged at Error level on every batch, including full ID lists (up to batch size), flooding logs and triggering false alerts (also lines 537, 554, 557, 576, 579).

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds multiple `r.log.Error(...)` calls inside the new per-batch cleanup loops (e.g., in `CleanAnnotations` for MaxAge/MaxCount and in `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags`), and these log fields include `"ids", ids` plus `"count", len(ids)` on every batch. Since these are unconditional (not gated on `err != nil`) and use Error level, they will emit error logs even on successful cleanup runs, potentially flooding logs and exposing large ID lists up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize`. This is an operational/logging-level issue introduced by the change, not a functional correctness defect in the cleanup logic itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:615 — Placeholder path has no per-dialect parameter cap, so large batch sizes exceed the limits on MSSQL (2100) and Postgres/MySQL (65535) and every cleanup run fails.

adjudication.rationale: The new `deleteByIDs` implementation builds an `IN` clause with one placeholder per ID for all non-SQLite dialects (`placeholders := "?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)`), and `ids` is sized up to `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` via `fetchIDs` using a `LIMIT`. There is no per-dialect cap (only a special-case for SQLite >999), so if `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configured above a database’s maximum parameter count (e.g., MSSQL’s 2100), `session.Exec` will error and each cleanup run can fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:607 — SQLite switch keys on configured batch size rather than len(ids) and hardcodes 999, inconsistent with the test's 32767 (SQLite >= 3.32.0) assumption.

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteByIDs`, the SQLite path uses a hardcoded `sqliteParameterLimit = 999` and switches based on `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` rather than `len(ids)`. While `len(ids)` is currently bounded by the batch size (because `fetchIDs` uses a `Limit(batchSize)`), making this unlikely to break correctness, it is still a concrete issue: it forces ID inlining even when the current batch has <=999 IDs (but configured batch size is larger), and it conflicts with the added test case that references SQLite supporting much larger variable counts (32767) — the code never attempts to use that capability and the 999 comment may be misleading/outdated for the tested scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — Cleanup ticker cut from 10m to 1m while each run can take up to 9m, so heavy delete jobs run nearly continuously against the DB.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the cleanup loop ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute (`time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` → `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`), which will make cleanup attempts significantly more frequent and could increase DB load if cleanup work is heavy. However, the claim that “each run can take up to 9m” and that delete jobs therefore run “nearly continuously” is not verifiable from this diff alone (no run-duration info shown), so it’s a real diff-grounded concern but not a proven defect from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:611 — Repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation to build the inline SQLite ID list is O(n^2) for large batches; use strings.Builder/Join.

adjudication.rationale: In xorm_store.go `deleteByIDs`, the SQLite branch builds `values` by repeatedly doing `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop. This reallocates and copies the growing string each iteration, making it O(n^2) for large `ids` batches (e.g., `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` can be 32767 per the added test). It’s a performance/scalability issue, not a functional correctness bug, and is directly grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:83 — Subtests now reseed and wipe the DB each time, so "running the max count delete again" no longer runs a second cleanup and doesn't test idempotency the way its name says.

adjudication.rationale: In the refactored table-driven test, each subtest now calls `createTestAnnotations(...)` and registers a `t.Cleanup` that deletes from `annotation`/`annotation_tag`, so subtests no longer share state. The case named "running the max count delete again..." only runs `cleaner.Run(...)` once and seeds `createAnnotationsNum: 9` (i.e., already at `MaxCount: 3` per type), so it no longer exercises a second cleanup pass/idempotency as its name implies; it now tests the "already at limit" scenario instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:98 — The test name mentions SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER (32766), but the code branches at 999, and no test covers a batch size between 2 and 999 or right at the 999/1000 boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The added test case is named "should not fail if batch size is larger than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER..." and uses batch size 32767, but the production branch in `deleteByIDs` is keyed off a hardcoded SQLite parameter limit of 999 (`const sqliteParameterLimit = 999` and `if ... AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit`). This makes the test name misleading relative to the actual logic being exercised. Also, the tests only use batch size 1 and 32767, so the boundary behavior around 999/1000 (where the branch flips between placeholders vs inlined IDs) is not covered by the new/updated tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:41 — Every other case uses batch size 1, so the multi-ID "?,?,..." placeholder path in deleteByIDs never runs with more than one ID.

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, all cases set `annotationCleanupJobBatchSize: 1` except the last, which sets `32767` (and is explicitly for SQLite). With batch size 1, `fetchIDs(... Limit(1))` yields at most one ID, so `deleteByIDs`’s placeholder branch (`"?" + strings.Repeat(",?", len(ids)-1)`) never exercises the multi-placeholder case. In the large-batch SQLite case, `deleteByIDs` takes the SQLite-specific inline-ID SQL path (`r.db.GetDBType()==migrator.SQLite && ... > 999`), so the multi-`?,?` placeholder logic still isn’t covered. This is a specific, diff-grounded test-coverage gap for the newly added deletion logic, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:357 — The new untilDoneOrCancelled, fetchIDs (empty-condition error) and deleteByIDs error/cancellation paths have no tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new helper logic in xorm_store.go: untilDoneOrCancelled (context-cancellation loop), fetchIDs (explicit error on empty condition), and deleteByIDs (two code paths: SQLite inline-IDs vs placeholders, plus session Exec/RowsAffected error handling). The updated cleanup_test.go adds integration coverage for the large SQLite batch-size success case (exercising the SQLite inline-IDs branch indirectly) and general cleanup success behavior, but it does not add targeted tests for the new error/cancellation paths (e.g., ctx cancellation in untilDoneOrCancelled, fetchIDs called with empty condition, or deleteByIDs Exec/RowsAffected errors). This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:241 — createTestAnnotations now inserts explicit IDs starting at 1, which skips the Postgres sequence and can cause PK collisions or hide ordering bugs, and it only works because every subtest wipes the table.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly sets `a.ID = int64(i+1)` in `createTestAnnotations` (cleanup_test.go) and inserts via `InsertMulti`, which bypasses any auto-increment/sequence mechanism a real DB (e.g., Postgres) might use. The test relies on per-subtest cleanup (`DELETE FROM annotation` / `annotation_tag`) to avoid immediate PK collisions when reusing IDs starting at 1. While an actual collision with a Postgres sequence isn’t directly demonstrated in this diff (it depends on how the test DB/sequence is initialized and whether later inserts omit IDs), the change does introduce a concrete test robustness concern tied to explicit PK assignment and table-only cleanup (no sequence reset).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:120 — t.Cleanup is registered after seeding and require calls, so a failed seed skips cleanup and leaves rows that later subtests pick up.

adjudication.rationale: In TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp, fakeSQL is initialized once outside the subtests and reused. Inside each t.Run, the database is seeded (createTestAnnotations) and assertions are made before t.Cleanup is registered. If createTestAnnotations or the early asserts fail via require/assert, the t.Cleanup registration is never reached, so rows in annotation/annotation_tag remain and can affect later subtests that share the same DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:99 — The 40003-row case runs on every DB backend inside a table test, which adds a lot of integration time and may be flaky under timeouts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a table-driven integration test case that creates 40,003 annotations (`createAnnotationsNum: 40003`) in `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp` and runs it unconditionally within the loop over `tests` (no gating by DB type/dialect). This will significantly increase runtime for that integration test and could contribute to timeout/flakiness. The claim that it runs on “every DB backend” isn’t directly verifiable from the diff alone (depends on what `db.InitTestDB(t)` does in CI), but the large-row case is clearly part of the normal integration test execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:108 — The large-batch case only has old-by-count annotations (createOldAnnotationsNum 0), so the MaxAge path with the inlined-ID SQLite branch never runs.

adjudication.rationale: In the new large-batch test case, `cfg` uses `settingsFn(0, 1)` for all types (i.e., `MaxAge == 0`, `MaxCount == 1`), and `createOldAnnotationsNum` is `0`, so `CleanAnnotations`’s `if cfg.MaxAge > 0 { ... }` branch is definitely not exercised. While the SQLite inlined-ID logic is in `deleteByIDs` (used by both MaxAge and MaxCount paths), this test only drives the MaxCount cleanup path with a large batch size and does not cover the MaxAge cleanup path under the same SQLite parameter-limit conditions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 — The cleanup ticker interval changed from 10m to 1m (a behaviour change) with no test and no config.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go changes the ticker interval from 10 minutes to 1 minute (`time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` → `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`), which is a concrete behavior change. The diff does not show any corresponding configuration option or test update to justify/guard this change, so the review concern is specific and diff-grounded, but it’s not verifiably a defect from the diff alone (could be intentional).
